title: Main Idea — Practice B: Stated Idea
subject: rla
author: Chee Skool
reviewer: C4 Main Idea editorial review pending
reviewNotes: Stated-main-idea transfer using a source-faithful CC-BY adaptation. Final summary removed so the passage structure—not a repeated conclusion—carries the answer.

curriculum.learningObjective: Identify a stated main idea and verify how later details develop it.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that most directly states the overall idea developed by the rest of the passage.

targets.text: Sleep supports how well teenagers function each day by affecting their brains, emotions, and bodies.
During sleep, the brain organizes information from the day and prepares for the next one.

explanation.whyCorrect: The opening sentence names the three major branches developed by the rest of the passage: brain, emotions, and physical health.
explanation.quickTip: A stated main idea often predicts the structure that follows.

questions.hint: Look for the sentence broad enough to cover all three later branches.

questions.prompt: Match each supporting detail to the branch of the stated main idea it develops.

items.text: Poor sleep can make it harder to remember information, pay attention, solve problems, and make decisions.
Stress, anxiety, irritability, frustration, and low mood can feel stronger.
Too little sleep can weaken the immune system and make it harder to fight illness.

explanation.answer: Brain: i1; Emotions: i2; Physical health: i3.
explanation.whyCorrect: Each detail develops one of the three branches named in the opening sentence: brain, emotions, or physical health.
explanation.quickTip: Ask how each detail helps develop the stated main idea, not merely whether it is true.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the passage as a whole?

options.text: Sleep mainly helps teenagers remember information and make better decisions.
options.whyWrong: This covers only the brain branch and leaves out emotional and physical health.

options.text: Sleep affects teenagers’ cognitive, emotional, and physical functioning, so getting enough sleep supports how well they function overall.
Poor sleep can make it harder for teenagers to fight illness.
options.whyWrong: This is one physical-health detail, not the whole passage.

options.text: Getting enough sleep prevents emotional and physical health problems in teenagers.
options.whyWrong: The passage describes effects and risks, but it does not claim enough sleep prevents all such problems.

explanation.whyCorrect: It covers all three major branches—thinking, emotions, and physical health—without turning one detail into the whole passage or making an absolute claim.
explanation.quickTip: A main idea should cover the major branches, not just repeat a true detail.

description: Stated-main-idea practice using a teen-sleep source adaptation.
